Net-yield durability through shocks and normalization - whether CCL sustains ~2-3% net yield growth on deliberately low ~1-3% capacity to keep the PROPEL deleveraging/EPS-growth algorithm intact (net debt/EBITDA -> 2.75x/BBB, EPS +50% vs 2025 by 2029), versus the recurring fuel/geopolitical swing factor (2026 Middle East already cut FY2026 normalized yield guidance from ~2.75% to ~2.25% and knocked $500M off EBITDA) plus softening consumer sentiment dragging yields back toward the pre-COVID guide-then-cut pattern.
